root.name: Latvian Gambit: Clam Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d3 f5 4. exf5

overview: White avoids the main Latvian with 3.d3, and after 3...f5 4.exf5 has taken the pawn. Black has given the f-pawn and aims for ...e4 or ...d5 with quick development. White has a healthy extra pawn and a solid set-up, so this is a poor version of an already dubious opening for Black.

white_ideas.idea: Take the pawn, then consolidate with Nc3, Be2 and castling
Return the pawn at a good moment to stay safe

black_ideas.idea: Open the e-file with ...e4 or ...d5 and play for development
Target f5 and use pins against the f3 knight

typical_structures.structure: Black open f- and e-files against a solid White set-up

character.notes: Black plays for tactics a pawn down, while the White king is not under direct fire.

gambit.notes: White keeps the pawn after 4.exf5 if he consolidates; ...e4 only gives Black development.

soundness.notes: The Latvian Gambit is on the dubious list, and this is an easier version for White.

structure.notes: Both ...e4 and ...d5 open the centre quickly.

approach.notes: Part of the Latvian, which strong players hardly ever use.

level.notes: Not a good repertoire choice, and White simply develops.

character.reason: Black is a pawn down and plays for forcing tactics down the open files.

gambit.reason: Black gives the f-pawn and White can keep it.

soundness.reason: The Latvian family is considered unsound and this move order adds no extra justification.

structure.reason: Trades on e4 or d5 open the position.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly ever play the Latvian.

level.reason: A dubious line cannot be beginner, and the plan is clear but unsound.

plans.reason: Black hopes faster development justifies the pawn.
